body.text: Northern Nepal’s devastating floods have brought renewed focus on climate risks, fragile mountain ecosystems and the challenges South Asia faces in preparing for large-scale disasters.

On August 26, a deadly flood hit northern Nepal, killing thousands, leaving thousands missing, and sweeping away entire villages. The disaster has drawn attention to the region’s vulnerability to extreme weather and raised a larger question: is South Asia prepared to deal with disasters of this scale?

This Frontline Webinar examines the region’s disaster management frameworks, resources and policies. In the latest edition of the Frontline webinar, Vedaant Lakhera speaks with Vinod Kumar Gaur, Honorary Emeritus Scientist at CSIR-National Institute of Data Science & AI, Bengaluru; Himanshu Thakkar, Coordinator of SANDRP; and Rishika Pardikar, environment and climate reporter.
The discussion looked at the science behind the Nepal floods, the state of disaster preparedness across South Asia, and the need for stronger regional cooperation.
